title_it: Il Mercato del Lavoro Credenzialista in Italia: Coerenza Studi-Lavoro, Sovraistruzione e Brain Waste
title_en: The Credentialist Labor Market in Italy: Job-Study Coherence, Over-Education, and Brain Waste
theoretical_framework: Randall Collins (Credential Society) & Gary Becker (Human Capital Theory vs Screening/Signaling)
core_empirical_paradox: In standard economic theory, a country with a scarcity of university graduates (`Italy has only 29.2% tertiary attainment among 25-34 year olds, vs 43.1% EU average`) should exhibit intense employer demand, high job-study coherence, and substantial wage premiums for degree holders. Instead, Italy exhibits the exact opposite: the lowest share of graduates (`scarcity`), yet the lowest employment coherence in the entire European Union (`41.6% coherence, ranking last in UE-27`), alongside high over-education (`58.4% mismatch`) and stagnant starting wages (`~€1,420 net/month`).

causal_explanation_in_extended_triangle.step: 1. Enterprise Dwarfism & Low High-Tech Demand ($D$ Barrier)
causal_explanation_in_extended_triangle.mechanism: Italian production is dominated by micro-enterprises (<5 employees) in traditional manufacturing, tourism, and services. These firms rarely engage in advanced R&D and lack the organizational structure to absorb complex scientific/academic human capital.

causal_explanation_in_extended_triangle.step: 2. Degrees as Screening Credentials Rather Than Human Capital ($E \rightarrow D$ Mismatch)
causal_explanation_in_extended_triangle.mechanism: Because employers lack specialized high-tech roles, they use university degrees (`Lauree`) and Liceo diplomas purely as 'screening credentials' (`segnalazione di conformità e disciplina`) to hire candidates for generic administrative, clerical, or service jobs (`mismatch verticale / over-education`).

Italian tracking pushes massive cohorts into theoretical Humanities/Legal faculties (`>48% mismatch`) without parallel investment in high-level technological academies (`ITS Academy`). Consequently, youth acquire credentials that do not align with regional labor market realities (`mismatch orizzontale`).

comparative_metrics.structural_classification: Extreme Credentialism & Structural Brain Waste (`Lowest EU Coherence, High Over-education despite Scarcity of Graduates`)
High Coherence & Dual-System Alignment (`Strong VET absorption, Low Mismatch`)
Moderate Mismatch (`High tertiary participation with institutionalized Grand Ecoles absorption`)
High Over-Education (`Over-supply of tertiary degrees relative to tourism/service labor demand`)

disciplinary_metrics.overeducation_risk: Low (`High enterprise technical demand, though wages lag EU peers`)
Moderate (`Absorption in banking/services, but often in generic administrative clerical roles`)
High (`Severe over-supply; >40% work in roles where law degree was not formally required or utilized`)
Severe (`Nearly 1 in 2 graduates work in non-coherent service/clerical jobs due to limited teaching/cultural vacancies`)
